findings.title: Persist the parsed credentials rather than the safeParse result
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result, { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous parse call returned the credentials themselves. Saving this result as credential.key removes access_token and refresh_token from the top level. After any successful Google token refresh, including with syncing disabled, the next GoogleCalendarService construction will fail googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key). Persist the result's data instead.

findings.title: The computed schema keys do not preserve token response fields
findings.body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema produces an ordinary string key (typically '[object Object]'), not a wildcard property validator. Both computed keys collide, and z.object strips unrecognized properties by default. With syncing enabled, expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token and other real response fields are therefore discarded. Zoom subsequently computes an invalid expiry from undefined, and Office 365 loses its refreshed expiry. Define explicit expiry fields and preserve the required provider fields rather than using schema objects as property names.

findings.title: Normalize sync responses for SDK and Axios callers
findings.body: The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but several newly wrapped callers expect a different result shape: Google reads res.data, Zoho CRM and Bigin read tokenInfo.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly. A fetch Response exposes none of these properties, regardless of its JSON body. Consequently these integrations throw or use undefined tokens whenever syncing is enabled. Decode and adapt the sync response at each caller, or establish a consistent decoded return contract for the helper.

findings.title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy value
findings.body: This fallback also runs when credential syncing is disabled. Office 365 explicitly permits refresh responses without refresh_token and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. Previously that preserved the existing refresh token; now it overwrites it with the literal 'refresh_token'. The next refresh then fails and the user must reconnect. Leave omitted refresh tokens absent so callers can retain the existing value.

findings.title: Import the Prisma client before using it
findings.body: The new refresh path calls prisma.credential.update, but this file has no prisma import or declaration. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws ReferenceError after a successful token response, preventing Salesforce client initialization.

findings.title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
findings.body: Unlike the other integrations, Salesforce unconditionally refreshes directly against login.salesforce.com and never uses CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. In the new source-of-truth setup, where the parent application owns refresh tokens and supplies access tokens, this request fails before a connection can be constructed. Even when a local refresh token exists, this bypasses the parent application's token management. Use the sync-aware refresh path and initialize the connection with the returned credentials.

findings.title: Pass the user ID instead of the credential ID to token syncing
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens interprets its third argument as a user ID and sends it as calcomUserId. Bigin passes credentialId, which identifies a credential row rather than its owner. When the IDs differ, the parent application either cannot find the user or returns another user's Bigin token, potentially causing CRM writes to the wrong account. Carry credential.userId into this method and pass that instead; team credentials should retain the null-user fallback.

findings.title: Send Zoom's app slug rather than its integration directory name
findings.body: The sync request sends appSlug='zoomvideo', but Zoom credentials are created with appId='zoom' in the callback, and the incoming credential webhook resolves apps by their stored slug. A parent application keyed by the same app slug used to push credentials will not find 'zoomvideo', so Zoom refresh syncing fails. Pass 'zoom' here.
